$comment: Canonical control taxonomy for the IaCSecBench finding-normalization engine.
Each entry defines one canonical control and lists the native rule identifiers
that each evaluated tool emits for it. The normalization engine uses this file
to decide whether a tool's finding corresponds to the violation a benchmark
case was authored to contain.
The 'verified' field records whether the rule-identifier mapping has been
confirmed against actual tool output on this corpus. Entries are seeded from
published rule catalogues and MUST be confirmed before results are reported:
run 'python -m evaluation.normalize --emit-unmapped' after a baseline run to
list every rule identifier the tools actually emitted but this file does not
cover, then extend the map and flip 'verified' to true.
Unmapped findings are never silently discarded. They are counted and reported,
because a tool that detects a violation under a rule identifier absent from
this file would otherwise be scored as a false negative -- which would bias
the comparison in favour of the reference implementation.
An entry must not name a rule identifier the tool cannot emit. Seven 'opa'
identifiers previously listed here (api_gateway_authorization,
hardcoded_credential, k8s_privileged_container, k8s_run_as_non_root,
k8s_resource_limits, oidc_audience_binding, pii_present) matched no rule in
security_framework/policies/*.rego. Such an entry cannot produce a false
detection -- nothing emits the identifier -- but it overstates how many
controls the reference policy set covers, which is precisely the direction of
error that flatters the reference. They were removed rather than implemented,
so the map now describes the policy set that exists.
Check this invariant after editing:
the 'opa' list of every control must be a subset of the "rule_id"
literals in security_framework/policies/*.rego.
Two further checkov identifiers were corrected against the installed
catalogue ('checkov --list', version 3.3.8): CKV_K8S_23 and CKV_K8S_40 do not
exist in it and were replaced by CKV_K8S_6 ('Do not admit root containers');
CKV_K8S_13 is 'Memory requests should be set', a requests check that had been
mapped to a limits control, and was replaced by CKV_K8S_12 ('Memory Limits
should be set'). ID_WEAK_TOKEN_VALIDATION and PII_UNMASKED_PERSONAL_DATA were
removed: both lost their only rule with the phantom OPA identifiers, no tool
could report them, and no case exercises them.
Eight controls retain verified=false, each naming its single uncorroborated
identifier in 'unverified_identifiers'. All eight are tfsec long IDs that could
not be confirmed in this environment: tfsec 1.28.14 has no check-listing
command, and '--include-passed' only surfaces checks whose target resource type
appears in the scanned corpus -- which contains no API Gateway and no Kubernetes
resources at all. '--filter-results' is not a test either: it returns zero
results for an unknown identifier and for a real-but-untriggered one alike.
They are retained rather than deleted because a wrong identifier here is inert:
nothing emits it, so it never matches, and the only possible effect of keeping
it is to credit tfsec if the identifier turns out to be real. Deleting it could
only ever under-credit a comparator. Where the two options differ, the one that
cannot flatter the reference implementation is the one to take.
STO_UNENCRYPTED_BUCKET was retitled after an independent relabelling pass
disagreed on STO-UNENCRYPTED-BUCKET-VULN. Its stated text ('lacks server-side
encryption') is satisfied by SSE-S3, but the case labels an AES256 bucket as
violating, which is only correct under a customer-managed-key requirement. The
text was corrected to match the label rather than the label to match the text,
because requiring a CMK is a defensible control and is what the corpus, the
policy set and the tfsec/checkov CMK rules all actually test. Note that this
makes the control stricter than CIS AWS 2.1.1, which the 'note' field records.

STO_PUBLIC_BUCKET.title: Object storage bucket permits public access

STO_UNENCRYPTED_BUCKET.title: Object storage bucket not encrypted with a customer-managed key
STO_UNENCRYPTED_BUCKET.note: Stricter than the CIS control it cites. CIS AWS 2.1.1 requires encryption at rest and is satisfied by SSE-S3 (sse_algorithm = AES256); this control additionally requires a customer-managed KMS key, matching MON_NO_LOG_ENCRYPTION. The previous title, 'Object storage bucket lacks server-side encryption', described the weaker CIS requirement while the corpus labelled an AES256 bucket as violating -- the one disagreement found by independent relabelling. The title now states the requirement the label actually encodes.

STO_NO_ACCESS_LOGGING.title: Object storage bucket lacks access logging

NET_UNRESTRICTED_INGRESS.title: Security group permits unrestricted ingress from 0.0.0.0/0

NET_PUBLIC_INSTANCE.title: Compute instance assigned a public address

IAM_WILDCARD_ACTION.title: Identity policy grants wildcard actions or resources

IAM_WILDCARD_TRUST.title: Role trust policy permits assumption by any principal

ENC_UNENCRYPTED_VOLUME.title: Block storage volume unencrypted at rest

ENC_UNENCRYPTED_DATABASE.title: Managed database storage unencrypted at rest

ENC_NO_KEY_ROTATION.title: Key management key lacks automatic rotation

MON_NO_TRAIL_VALIDATION.title: Audit trail lacks log file integrity validation

MON_TRAIL_NOT_MULTIREGION.title: Audit trail not enabled across all regions

MON_NO_LOG_ENCRYPTION.title: Log group unencrypted with customer-managed key

CMP_NO_IMDSV2.title: Compute instance permits unauthenticated metadata access

CMP_NO_IMAGE_SCANNING.title: Container registry lacks image vulnerability scanning

CMP_MUTABLE_IMAGE_TAGS.title: Container registry permits mutable image tags

SEC_HARDCODED_CREDENTIAL.title: Credential material embedded in configuration source

K8S_ROOT_CONTAINER.title: Container permitted to run as root

K8S_NO_RESOURCE_LIMITS.title: Container lacks CPU or memory limits

NET_NO_HTTPS_REDIRECT.title: Content delivery endpoint does not enforce HTTPS redirection

NET_ALB_INVALID_HEADERS.title: Load balancer does not drop invalid header fields
